correctness.rationale: The maximum is interior since a transfer to a zero coordinate improves the objective. Equal marginal derivatives and positive second variation between any two coordinates above 2 leave only equality or one v>2 and m−1 equal coordinates u∈(1,2). For fixed unequal high fraction p, the objective divided by the equal objective is strictly convex in stock, starts at one with negative derivative and tends to infinity, so there is one positive crossing. Solving at t=(v−u)/m gives p=1/A_m(t) and crossing stock m(m−1)tA_m(t)/(m−A_m(t)); the parameter ranges bijectively over the unequal fractions. For two habitats this crossing-stock function is 2t coth(t/2), strictly greater than 4 and tending to 4 at zero; the unequal-optimum half-gap z satisfies z coth z=s/2−1 and vanishes at onset. For m≥3 the crossing-stock expansion is 2m[1−(m−2)t/6+O(t²)] at zero and the function grows like mt at infinity. Thus it attains its minimum below 2m at positive t. At that tie the asymmetric allocation is a genuine global maximizer, so its v>2 gives s_m>2 and a positive separation from equality; above s_m an asymmetric maximizer retains v>2, so the separation persists as s decreases to s_m. At large stock v=s−(m−1)u→∞, so equality of marginal derivatives forces u→1, proving the stated limit and ratio. These are analytic checks of the continuum claim under identical independent habitats, not a behavioral or empirical interpretation. The reported numerical diagnostics were inspected but not executed.
